signature.name: Georgia Aquarium
signature.detail: One of the largest aquariums in the world and Atlanta's top draw, with whale sharks and beluga whales among its headline exhibits. Book timed-entry tickets online in advance, especially for weekends and school holidays, and arrive early to beat the crowds.

signature.name: World of Coca-Cola
signature.detail: A museum devoted to the famous soft drink, next to Centennial Olympic Park, with tasting rooms and company history. Allow a couple of hours and buy tickets online to skip the queue.

signature.name: Centennial Olympic Park
signature.detail: A downtown park built for the 1996 Olympics, with the Fountain of Rings as its centerpiece. It is free and open daily; visit in the late afternoon for cooler weather and the fountain shows.

signature.name: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park
signature.detail: Preserves the birthplace, church and legacy of Martin Luther King Jr., making it essential for understanding the city's civil rights history. Entry to the park sites is free; check hours for the birth home and visitor center before you go.

signature.name: High Museum of Art
signature.detail: Atlanta's leading art museum, known for its collection and striking buildings in Midtown. It is closed on some weekdays, so check the schedule and consider a combined ticket if offered.

signature.name: Atlanta Botanical Garden
signature.detail: A large garden next to Piedmont Park with seasonal displays and a canopy walk. Go in the morning for cooler temperatures and easier parking.

signature.name: Fox Theatre
signature.detail: A historic 1920s theater with an ornate Moorish-inspired interior, hosting shows and tours. Check the calendar for performances or guided tours, and book ahead for popular acts.

transport: MARTA ride about $2.50; rideshares $15-30 across downtown
